texts.preamble: M/S.Janasevana Nyayavila Bazaar Pvt. ... vs The District Police Chief on 30 August, 2017 Author: K.Vinod Chandran Bench: K.Vinod Chandran In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam Present: The Honourable Mr.Justice K.Vinod Chandran & The Honourable Mr. Justice Ashok Menon Monday, The 12Th Day Of February 2018 / 23Rd Magha, 1939 WP(C).No. 694 of 2018(J) ------------------------- Petitioner(S): -------------- M/S.Janasevana Nyayavila Bazaar Pvt. Ltd. Having Office 1St Floor, Door No.1361, Puliyazhikathu Plaza, Trivandrum Road, Pulamon P.O., Kottarakara, Kollam District-691531, Represented By Its Managing Director, Hafees. By Adv.Sri.Manu Ramachandran Respondent(S): -------------- 1. The District Police Chief, Kollam Rural Police Having Office At Kottarakara, Kollam District. 2. The Deputy Superintendent Of Police, Punalur, Kollam. 3. The Sub Inspector Of Police, Kottarakara Police Station, Kollam District. 4. The Sub Inspector Of Police, Kunnickode Police Station, Kollam District.
texts.facts: The party respondents herein are said to be persons, who have entered into agreements with the petitioner. The petitioner having taken a security deposit from the franchisees, in proportion to the extent of the shop buildings offered by the franchisees, has carried out interior works and has also supplied materials for sale in the franchisee's unit. The arrangement was that the sale price would be remitted to the petitioner company and the franchisees would be given a monthly remuneration. The petitioner's contention is that the WP(C) 694/2018 franchisees themselves started selling their own products within the shops and failed to deposit the amounts due to the petitioner company. Not only that the 12th respondent is said to have ransacked the petitioner's premises and taken away many goods. The petitioner lodged a complaint as seen from Ext.P5 and also gave a representation to the District Police Chief apprehending that the other franchisees would repeat what the 12 th respondent did. 2. Respondents 5, 6, 8 and 11 do not appear. The Writ Petition has been filed merely on an apprehension. It is also the submission of respondents 7, 9 and 10 that there has been serious misappropriation of funds by the petitioner on the basis of the so-called chain of super markets and that huge amounts were taken from the party respondents, who have filed complaints before the respective police stations. It is also the specific WP(C) 694/2018 contention of the party respondents that the complaints together has to result in an investigation by the Special Branch CID as per Circular No.22/2013 as an economic offence, since the amounts involved exceed Rs.2 crores. It is submitted that respondents 7, 9 and 10 have filed complaints and so would the others. 3. The 12th respondent categorically submits that there was no incident of a ransacking of the petitioner's premises. In fact, the 12th respondent, dissatisfied with the franchisee agreement, had taken the goods supplied by the petitioner company back to his premises, which was refused. These goods were taken back in two lorries on the basis of which a complaint was raised by the petitioner.
texts.arguments: Advocate Shri D.Kishore appearing for respondents 7, 9 and 10 specifically points out that there is no allegation against any of the party respondents, but the 12th respondent. The learned Counsel for the party respondents also submits that they do not propose to take law into their hands.
texts.petitioner_arguments: Advocate Shri D.Kishore appearing for respondents 7, 9 and 10 specifically points out that there is no allegation against any of the party respondents, but the 12th respondent. The learned Counsel for the party respondents also submits that they do not propose to take law into their hands.
